messages.subject: More questions about Dail and Madsen (2011) generalized N-mixture model
parts:
Hello unmarked people! I have some questions regarding the generalized N-mixture model of Dail and Madsen (2011).


First of all, here is my model:

model_sky <- pcountOpen(~1, ~1, ~1, ~Cloud, data = umf_sky, mixture = "ZIP", K = 100, dynamics = "autoreg", fix = "none", se = TRUE)


Here are my population parameter estimates:

lam_sky <- exp(coef(model_sky, type="lambda")) #Gives 2.96
gam_sky <- exp(coef(model_sky, type="gamma")) #Gives 0.15
om_sky <- plogis(coef(model_sky, type="omega")) #Gives 0.88
p_sky <- plogis(coef(model_sky, type="det")) #Gives  0.44


#Population size season 1:

model_sky_re <- ranef(model_sky)
year1_sky <- sum(bup(model_sky_re)) #Gives 248


If I understand this correctly, I have a population size of 248 skylarks in the first season, with an average abundance of 2.96 individuals per surveyed point. The recruitment rate (reproduction and immigration) is 0.15, which means that 0.15×248=37.2 individuals will join the population in the second season. The survival probability (deaths and emigration) is 0.88, which means that 0.88×248=218.24 individuals will die or leave between the first and second season. But this seems too simple…


Now my questions:


1.       What is the actual equation for recruitment rate and survival probability that the functions calculates? I used auto-regression and ZIP distribution in my model.

2.       I have 83 survey sites, so why does sum(bup()) give me 248 and not 2.96×83=245.68?

3.       Is “survival probability” defined as “deaths + emigration”, or as “1 – (deaths + emigration)”?

4.       How do I calculate my population size (and standard deviations and conf. int.) for year 2, 3, 4 and 5? It can’t be as simple as my calculation above I guess.


Thanks a lot and sorry for very basic questions! I appreciate even if you only answer some of them.


(And yes, I have consulted the Dail and Madsen article as well as the unmarked instructions, but I’m afraid it’s a bit too technical/mathematical for me at the moment)

messages.author: 4a15de51da4445ae
messages.subject: Re: [unmarked] More questions about Dail and Madsen (2011) generalized N-mixture model
parts:
hi Krisztina,
 1. The recruitment autoreg model is simply R ~ Poisson(N*gamma) (see the Hostetler and Chandler 2015 Ecology paper for a discussion of various recruitment models) and the default survival model is simply binomial(N, phi). I would share the proofs of the AHM2 chapter on open models if you send me a direct email (we should have revised proofs in a week or so...).
 2. the BUP is based on the estimated posterior distribution of N for each site. This is not ever equal to nsites*E(N) either mathematically or conceptually.
 3. Survival probability is defined as in (1) above:  Survivors ~ Binomial(N, phi). Thus the number that don't survive is N - Survivors. I think the interpretation of mortality as individuals that die or emigrate is correct.
 4. I think SEs and CIs for derived parameters like population size would have to be based on a bootstrap since they are very complicated functions of the MLEs.  I haven't seen anyone do this so I don't have any specific guidance on this, sorry!

regards
andy

1. About the survival model, is Phi in this case refering to the "estimated trend in population size for a particular site", N(it)/N(it-1) (Dail & Madsen, 2011)? I am asking because in the unmarked documentation, this can also refer to the right-hand sided formula for availability, but I think that is true for other models and not the generalized N-mixture.

2. Okay I see, I did not know that. But is there some handy way to calculate estimated popsizes for the rest of the seasons then? For example in my data I have 5 seasons but as I understand, the BUP gives me popsize for season 1.

3. Great, thanks!

4. So when writing a scientific paper (or in this case my master thesis), it is not standard procedure to present CIs and SEs for those parameters? It is enough to just write the estimated omega, gamma, popsize, and so on? Because my problem with the bootstrap is that neither my own laptop nor the computers at my ecology department can handle the amount of data that I have, so I haven't been able to run a full bootstrap. Either R crashes or the analysis is terminated because I need to leave it overnight due to the massive amount of time it takes. So in that case I will simply not be able to present and CIs and SEs I guess.
